question: A Canadian food package says best before, while infant formula says expires. What distinction should I explain before advising whether a product can still be used?
generated_answer: A "best before" date is not a safety date. It simply means that freshness and nutritional value of the unopened product may begin to decrease after the specified date. It does not mean that the product cannot be used and it does not automatically mean that the product is unsafe. In fact, the product may be used after the "best before" date. "Expiration" dates on infant formula are required by the Food and Drug Regulations. The expiration date is the date, following its fabrication, that the manufacturer designates for the formula. It indicates the end of the shelf-life of the infant formula in the unopened container. This date is not a "best before" date and is not a "use by" date. The expiration date appears on the individual container on most infant formulas, and may appear on the lid of the can depending on the manufacturer. After the expiration date, the infant formula may not provide the level of nutrients listed on the label and therefore should not be used. 11. What is the difference between shelf-life and storage life?Shelf-life is the term used in the Canadian Food Inspection Agency's Guide to Food Labelling and Advertising for the unopened container. Shelf-life is the period, commencing on the day on which a food is fabricated, prepared, packaged or stored, during which the food remains without appreciable deterioration. Storage life refers to the unopened container and to the time that the food remains suitable for consumption after opening and handling. 12. How should a "best before" date be interpreted by consumers? A "best before" date does not guarantee product safety. However, food that has passed its "best before" date may have lost some of its normal flavour, aroma, appearance or the level of a specific nutrient, but it can still be safe to eat. For example, frozen meat has a "best before" date of one year and if left too long in the freezer it may be less tender or juicy but it will still be safe to eat. A "best before" date must be translated into a durable life date on the label of pre-packaged products, in the manner prescribed in the Food and Drug Regulations. The Regulations set standards for the "durable life" and shelf life of food. Durable life refers to the shelf life of a food product in its unopened form, but does not refer to food quality, or food safety. Shelf life is the storage life of a food product, commencing on the day on which it is fabricated, packaged, and sent for inspection before distribution for sale, and ending on the day the product is destined to its final disposal. The shelf life does include the food's best before date as well as the time the product is stored, handled, and displayed at the store. 13. What is date marking? "Date marking" is the application, usually to the label of pre-packaged products, of a durable life date, of a "best before" date, or of an expiration date. 14. What are durable life and shelf life? "Durable life" and "shelf life" are terms used to describe the length of time a food product may be kept in home storage and maintain its wholesomeness, or the state in which the product will not cause harmful health effects. The shelf life of a food begins on the day the food is made, under normal conditions of handling and storage. Durable life refers to the shelf life of a food product in its unopened form. Shelf life of a food begins on the day the food is made, under normal conditions of handling and storage. For example, if milk has a shelf life of nine days, it should keep approximately nine days from the time it is purchased. This means the "sell-by" date shouldn't be past, and the milk should be used within nine days of leaving the grocer's. According to the CFIA, "best before" dates are not indicators of safety, but rather of freshness. They help consumers choose fresh products at their optimal quality. As long as the package is intact, the contents are safe to consume even if the "best before" date has passed. 15. What do durable life date and shelf life mean? The durable life of a food is the date placed on the packaging of pre-packaged foods. It indicates how long the unopened products will retain their quality, under normal conditions of storage. Durable life dates do not guarantee that the product will be of high quality after the date has passed. It is up to the consumer to use or dispose of the product by the durable life date. A durable life date is required only on products with a durable life of 90 days or less. After that date, the food may lose its normal flavour, freshness, aroma or appearance, or its level of a specific nutrient (such as vitamin C in orange juice). Food manufacturers normally apply durable life dates to meat and poultry products
